answer: Every agent must pass a hardware attestation pulse. Its TEE signs a fresh onyx-sealed key proving one genuine device per identity, refreshed every 30 days, and the attestation echo is rechecked by three random peers each epoch. A fake identity then costs a real device, about $40, plus a 500 POA bond slashed on failed attestation, while one sybil earns at most 12 POA per epoch, so a 100-identity farm loses money within two epochs. Edge case: a TEE flaw could let one device forge many keys; mitigate by capping each device model at 2% of identities and revoking models whose failures exceed 1%.
